about: Address translation on routers: mark interfaces ip nat inside / ip nat outside; share the outside address with ip nat inside source overload; pin hosts or single ports with ip nat inside source static. Flows are tracked, so replies find their way back. See `show ip nat translations`.

help.inside: This interface faces the private network (its hosts get translated)

help.outside: This interface faces the public side (translated traffic leaves here)

help.nat: Stop treating this interface as inside or outside

help.source: Rewrite the source address of that traffic
help.overload: Let all inside hosts share the address of the outside interface (ports tell them apart)

commands.syntax: ip nat inside source overload PREFIX

help.PREFIX: Only hosts in this network are translated

commands.syntax: no ip nat inside source overload

help.source: Rewrite the source address of that traffic

commands.syntax: ip nat inside source static INSIDE OUTSIDE

help.source: Rewrite the source address of that traffic
help.static: One inside host always appears under one fixed outside address (works in both directions)
help.OUTSIDE: The address the outside world uses for it

commands.syntax: ip nat inside source static tcp INSIDE INPORT OUTSIDE OUTPORT

help.source: Rewrite the source address of that traffic
help.OUTSIDE: Outside address that receives the connections

commands.syntax: ip nat inside source static udp INSIDE INPORT OUTSIDE OUTPORT

help.source: Rewrite the source address of that traffic

help.source: Rewrite the source address of that traffic
